BIZ-0.reason_or_evidence: Authority-labelling rule (NY_STATUTE/NY_REGULATION/NYC_LAW/REBNY_UCBA/REBNY_RLS/NAR_MLS_POLICY/BROKERAGE_POLICY). No competing statement in PR #585 or PR #579. Governs how every other BIZ row may be described.

BIZ-1.reason_or_evidence: Three distinct effective dates (2024-01-01 decoupling, 2025-08-01 RLS field removal, 2026-01-20 UCBA revisions) that must not be merged. Sub-rules BIZ-1.1/1.2/1.3 carry the dates.

BIZ-2.reason_or_evidence: Pre-tour written agreement is an RLS/MLS participation rule, not a NY statute. Sub-rules BIZ-2.1 (not a boolean), 2.2 (4 behaviours), 2.3 (contents).

BIZ-3.reason_or_evidence: Decoupling changed the mechanism, not usually the payer. Establishes that compensation is a property of an executed agreement, never of a listing record — the premise BIZ-9 enforces.

BIZ-4.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: no `CompensationArrangement` model exists in prisma/schema.prisma. The nearest model, `CommissionPayment`, is DEAL-level (deal_id, payment_type, amount, status) and carries no agreement_id, no maximum_compensation and no objective_formula. It therefore cannot express BIZ-4.1 (transaction-level), BIZ-4.3 (enforced cap) or BIZ-4.5 (one receivable per agreement, never deal-level commission) — BIZ-4.5 is directly contradicted by the current shape. Gate: schema change requires explicit Maya approval.

BIZ-5.reason_or_evidence: Seven engagement types. Entitlement answered from the executed agreement, never inferred from activity.

BIZ-6.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED RISK: `CommissionPayment.status` defaults to "pending" with payment_type "received", and nothing observed ties either to a closing event. The invariant "never earned before closing" is therefore not enforced by the current schema; retained as a requirement the implementation must satisfy.

BIZ-7.reason_or_evidence: Commissions not set by law and fully negotiable; required content in listing agreements, buyer agreements and pre-closing documents. Attributed to REBNY_UCBA, not to NY law (BIZ-0).

BIZ-8.reason_or_evidence: Binds every generated and authored surface where compensation will be received from any source. Enforced via the compliance-sensitive surface list in POL-5.

BIZ-9.canonical_destination: §Business model — compensation never in listing content
BIZ-9.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: suppression exists and is real — lib/compliance/dto.ts:60-65 `REMOVED_FIELDS` lists the four RLS compensation fields; dto.ts:174-179 blanks nested `buyer.buyerAgentCompensation`/`Type`; lib/compliance/rebny-field-tables.ts:1162-1165 marks them `{raw:false, removed:true}`; lib/compliance/idx-display-gate.ts:93-94 blanks the DTO fields. NOT verified: that no export, feed, sitemap, report or campaign path bypasses these lists. Retained as an ACTIVE guard, not a historical note.
BIZ-9.dependency: BIZ-10 (fields still reachable in provider metadata)

BIZ-10.reason_or_evidence: REBNY removed compensation fields from the RLS on 2025-08-01; that did NOT remove them from Cotality/Trestle metadata, which spans multiple listing organizations. This is why BIZ-9 is an active guard.

BIZ-11.reason_or_evidence: NY requires agency-relationship disclosure; system records capacity per client relationship plus the disclosure event and date. Dual agency requires informed written consent; relationships never inferred from activity nor changed silently.

BIZ-12.reason_or_evidence: Rental engagements follow the same written-agreement principle subject to BIZ-2.2; fee responsibility follows the FARE Act rule in TXN-10, and unresolved fee attribution fails closed.

BIZ-13.reason_or_evidence: Nine-row register binding each rule to its governing source and effective date, keeping REBNY/RLS rules separate from NY statute and NYC law. This is the lookup BIZ-0 depends on.

ACT-1.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: the plan defines six actor classes (anonymous, client, agent, broker, system_job, service_identity). prisma/schema.prisma `model Session` carries only `user_type` ("agent"|"lead") plus a `role` string mixing staff and client roles ("BROKER"|"AGENT"|"buyer"|"tenant"|"seller"|"landlord"). system_job and service_identity have no representation.

ACT-2.reason_or_evidence: Client actors scoped by role AND resource; role alone never authorizes. Directly relevant to the audit finding AUDIT-PORTAL-ACTOR-SUBJECT, where routes reinterpret auth.userId as Lead.id.

ACT-3.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: an adapter layer exists (lib/auth/middleware.ts, lib/auth/index.ts, lib/portal/listing-ownership.ts all reference requirePortalRole). NOT verified: that no domain service re-derives identity from transport. Requirement retained as the rule that makes AUDIT-PORTAL-ACTOR-SUBJECT a defect rather than a style preference.

ACT-4.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED CONSISTENT: prisma `model Agent` carries license_type ("broker"|"salesperson") and Session.role admits both BROKER and AGENT, so one person holding both capacities is representable. Constrains every later feature: single-operator software that must not block multi-agent later.

ACT-5.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: `acting_capacity`/`actingCapacity` appears nowhere in lib/ or app/. No action records which capacity it was performed in, so audit history cannot distinguish a broker's producing action from a supervisory one — the precise distinction ACT-5 requires.

ACT-6.reason_or_evidence: A supervision requirement that would resolve to self-review is not enabled by default while the broker is the only producing agent. CMA-4 already applies this; ACT-6 generalizes it.

ACT-7.reason_or_evidence: Ownership field carried from the start and populated with the acting person; no backfill assumption. Conversely no routing/load-balancing/team-hierarchy/split-rule machinery before it is needed.

PER-1.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: no `Person` model exists in prisma/schema.prisma. `Lead` is the de-facto person record and carries `roles String[]` (buyer/renter/seller/landlord), which partially expresses multi-role, but lifecycle state lives on the Lead (`status`) rather than on the role — the exact conflation PER-1 forbids. Confirms deep-audit AUDIT-PERSON-ORG-IDENTITY. Gate: schema change requires explicit Maya approval.
PER-1.dependency: schema-migration hold; spine for SEA, SEL, CMA, MKT, TXN, CRM, INT

PER-2.reason_or_evidence: Email and telephone are supporting identifiers, never the sole identity key; identity resolution records confidence and merges are reversible with retained history. No merge-history structure exists today (no Person model).

PER-3.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: `FamilyMember` and `LeadParty` models exist and express some multi-party structure, but neither carries the decision-group attributes PER-3 requires (influence, legal authority, joint-approval requirements, document access, active dates).

PER-4.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: no `Organization` model exists. NYC transactions run through LLCs, trusts, estates, co-op corporations, managing agents, law firms, lenders and title companies; none is representable today, so a transaction counterparty cannot be an organization. Gate: schema change requires explicit Maya approval.

PER-5.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: PER-5 defines nine role states including `represented`. prisma `model Lead.status` defaults to "new" with documented values new/contacted/active/closed — four states, and no `represented`. `represented` is the precondition for agent-led tours under BIZ-2.2, so its absence means showing eligibility cannot currently be evaluated from state.

PER-6.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: `Lead.consent_captured_at` exists (TCPA/CAN-SPAM consent timestamp), so consent-at-capture is partly present. Full provenance (source, medium, campaign, landing surface, referring person/org, first-seen) not verified as a single immutable structure.

PER-7.reason_or_evidence: One accountable person at a time, recorded with assigning actor, timestamp and reason; reassignment appends rather than overwrites. `LeadAssignmentRule` exists in schema but append-only reassignment history was not verified.

PER-8.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED FRAGMENTATION: PER-8 requires ONE canonical append-only timeline per person. Today at least five separate event stores exist — `ActivityLog`, `PortalEvent`, `BehavioralEvent`, `IntentEvent`, `AuditEvent` — plus `OutreachEvent`. No single canonical timeline exists, and AuditEvent must not be repurposed as one (deep-audit AUDIT-WORKFLOW-OUTBOX).

PER-9.reason_or_evidence: Five knowledge types (verified fact, client-stated preference, observed behavior, broker hypothesis, confirmed decision) that are never silently promoted between. An inference is never presented as a statement. Directly governs INT-3 and every AI-generated surface.

PER-10.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: `FollowUpTask` exists and covers part of the shape, but PER-10 requires completion evidence, related interaction and related transaction so that "what Mallan owes this client" is answerable. Not verified as satisfied.

PER-11.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: `NotificationPreference` and `Lead.consent_captured_at` exist, but PER-11 requires consent to attach to the PERSON and survive role changes. With no Person model (PER-1), consent is attached to the Lead, so the stated guarantee — unsubscribed as a buyer stays unsubscribed when later a seller — is not structurally guaranteed.

PER-12.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED TENSION: `Session.user_type` is "agent"|"lead" and `Session.user_id` is a BigInt, so a portal session resolves to a Lead, not to a person holding roles. One person with two roles seeing both through one account is therefore not structurally guaranteed. Relates to deep-audit AUDIT-PORTAL-ACTOR-SUBJECT.

IAM-1.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: adapter layer present (lib/auth/middleware.ts, lib/auth/index.ts). Restates ACT-3 for the authentication path; kept as a DERIVED row rather than merged so the auth surface carries the rule explicitly.

IAM-2.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: IAM-2 requires four principal classes that never share a credential, session or authorization path. `model Session.user_type` admits only "agent"|"lead"; there is no service_principal, and staff/client roles are mixed in one `role` string column on one table. The "never share a session" guarantee is therefore not enforced at the schema level.

IAM-3.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: `model Session` records token, user_type, user_id, role, expires_at, created_at, ip_address, user_agent. It does NOT record the capacity in effect (ACT-5), last activity, or a revocation flag. IAM-3 requires revocation to take effect on the NEXT REQUEST rather than at next expiry; with only `expires_at` there is no observed mechanism for that.

IAM-4.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: an invitation flow exists — lib/email/templates.ts:82-86 builds `/portal/accept?token=...`. NOT verified: single-use enforcement, expiry, issuer recording, or fail-closed token validation. Self-registration must create a lead (PER-5), not a portal principal.

IAM-5.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: `model MfaSession` exists, so a stronger-assurance mechanism is present. NOT verified: that assurance level is RECORDED ON THE ACTION, which is the substantive half of IAM-5 (the mechanism itself is explicitly left as an implementation decision).

IAM-6.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PARTIAL: impersonation exists — app/api/auth/impersonation/stop/route.ts terminates an impersonation session and logs the end. NOT verified: that the session records BOTH principals, is time-bounded, is visible in audit history as impersonation, and cannot perform IAM-5 elevated actions.

IAM-7.reason_or_evidence: Tokens, secrets, session identifiers and credential material never appear in a response body, client-visible payload, log line, error message, URL or provider-bound telemetry. Enforcement is an audit obligation, not a single code site.

IAM-8.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PRESENT: lib/middleware/rate-limiter.ts exists. NOT verified: coverage of every unauthenticated surface named (public search, listing detail, autocomplete, lead capture, unsubscribe), nor attempt limits with lockout/backoff on authentication, invitation redemption and token validation. The ERR-2 requirement — a rate-limited response must never present as an empty result — is the compliance-critical half.

IAM-9.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED GAP: idempotency exists only in narrow places — lib/idx/media-sync.ts (listing_media upsert) and an ad-hoc duplicate check in app/api/crm/convert/route.ts:169. There is NO general idempotency-key contract for the operations IAM-9 names (offer submission, showing request, agreement execution, campaign release, arrangement creation, document upload), and no audit catches its absence.

IAM-10.reason_or_evidence: Source declares Status DECIDED for the requirement but OPEN for the concrete periods, tracked as Q-12. Governing constraints include NY SHIELD obligations and the retention period for executed agreements (BIZ-2.3). Carried forward as an open question — no period is chosen by assumption (AGT-6).

BRK-1.reason_or_evidence: Every capability available to an agent is available to the broker for the broker's own production; broker-only capability is additive, never a replacement. DERIVED from ACT-4 and kept as its own row because it constrains feature design directly.

BRK-2.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED SPLIT: the schema is largely present — prisma `model Agent` carries license_no, license_type, license_expiry, status and trestle_mls_id, plus ethics_training_expires_at. Ethics training IS enforced (lib/compliance/ethics-training-status.ts checks expiry NOT NULL and >= now). LICENSE expiry is NOT: every observed use of license_expiry is CRUD (app/api/crm/agents/me, /agents, /agents/[id]) with no blocking gate on capacity-bearing actions and no advance-of-expiry surfacing, which is what BRK-2 requires.

BRK-3.reason_or_evidence: Offboarding must revoke sessions (IAM-3), reassign accountable relationships (PER-7) and preserve history rather than delete it, never orphaning a client relationship, listing or open commitment. IAM-3 has no verified revocation mechanism, so this depends on that gap closing.

BRK-4.reason_or_evidence: Supervision surfaces (work requiring review, compliance exceptions, overdue commitments, unassigned leads, agreement gaps) become meaningful only when additional agents exist. Off by default per ACT-6; enabling them is configuration, not a rebuild.

BRK-5.reason_or_evidence: Fail-closed conditions must produce a VISIBLE OWNED exception rather than a silent block, each recording what failed, its authority (BIZ-0), the affected record, the owner and the resolution. This is the operational counterpart to the fail-closed rule and covers the BIZ-4.3 cap breach case.

BRK-6.reason_or_evidence: Explicit scope boundary: reports arrangements, expected receivables, earned commission at closing (BIZ-6), referral obligations and per-agent production; is NOT an accounting system, holds no funds (TXN-2), produces no tax filings and makes no legal or tax determinations. Export to an accountant is supported; being the ledger of record is not.

BRK-7.reason_or_evidence: Pipeline, inventory, lead-source performance, stage conversion, retention, referral sources and open commitments — each DRILLABLE to underlying records, never a figure without a path to its evidence. That drill-through constraint is the substantive requirement.

COT-1.reason_or_evidence: Cotality/Trestle controls transport, resources, fields, types, enums, relationships, pagination, throttling and errors for Mallan's licensed account. Foundational premise for the whole COT family and for CLAUDE.md §J (Codex is not live field authority).

COT-2.reason_or_evidence: Six-level precedence order placing the current effective REBNY rule first and dated reference documents / historical audits last. This is the tie-breaker every other reconciliation row depends on when sources disagree.

COT-3.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PRESENT: both commands exist — package.json:76 `cotality:pull` (scripts/cotality/pull-enums.mjs) and package.json:77 `cotality:verify` (scripts/cotality-verify.mjs). NOT verified: that a verification record captures all twelve required elements (verified_at, repository_sha, feed/license identity, metadata checksum, resources/fields/enums observed, filter and pagination probes, rejected operations, changes from prior). Rule that credentials-unavailable must be STATED, never guessed, is retained.

COT-4.canonical_destination: §Provider authority — field existence is not permission
COT-4.reason_or_evidence: A field appearing in the feed does not prove permission for public display, internal use, seller display, CMA use, analytics, storage, export or redistribution; the executed license and REBNY authorization govern. This is the rule that makes BIZ-10.1 (compensation fields present in metadata) non-alarming and BIZ-9 necessary.

COT-5.reason_or_evidence: Use only verified fields and values; never invent a provider field, enum, status, permission, media type or query behavior. Restated operationally by COT-11's prohibition list.

COT-6.reason_or_evidence: DIRECTLY VALIDATED BY OPS-024: the adapter must preserve BOTH the provider canonical key and the human/source listing identifier, and local code must not silently treat one as the other. The 2026-07-29 production incident was exactly this failure — SourceSystemKey was renamed to ListingKey after the fetch while the cursor layer read raw rows before the rename. Highest-priority row in the COT family.

COT-7.reason_or_evidence: Media relationships must use verified provider keys and exact provider URLs, never constructed by guessing; nine provenance attributes enumerated. Aligns with the REBNY rule that media uses ResourceRecordKey, not ResourceRecordID.

COT-8.reason_or_evidence: Preserve provider ordering, select the correct primary photo, distinguish photos/floor plans/videos/virtual tours, never substitute a floor plan as primary, retain provider timestamps, detect media-set changes, fail clearly when media is missing.

COT-9.reason_or_evidence: Every provider-derived output carries retrieval time, source modification time where available, and an explicit freshness state. Connects to SEA-8's `stale` search state.

COT-10.reason_or_evidence: Unknown values preserved raw, logged, reported and QUARANTINED from affected regulated outputs until classified; never silently mapped. The quarantine clause is the compliance-critical half — silent mapping is how a display gate gets the wrong answer.

COT-11.canonical_destination: §Provider authority — everything provider-derived is pulled live
COT-11.reason_or_evidence: Platform-wide blast radius, stated as such in the source. Enumerates seven prohibited shortcuts including copying a value from another market/provider/standards document/prior audit/code comment/agent memory, and inferring a value from a field name. This is the single most load-bearing provider rule and matches CLAUDE.md §J.3-J.5 (Codex is not authority for live field truth; B/C/D findings need independent proof).

COT-12.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PRESENT: package.json:77 `cotality:verify` exists as the drift check. Any committed copy of provider vocabulary is a cache, never an authority. Exit 0 = matches live, 1 = drift, 2 = unreachable. NOT verified in this session: that the script's exit codes match this contract.

COT-13.reason_or_evidence: Exit 2 means UNVERIFIED, not confirmed-unchanged. Work depending on provider truth stops rather than proceeding on the cached copy. This is a fail-closed rule and matches the CLAUDE.md §E fail-closed instruction.

COT-14.reason_or_evidence: Detected drift blocks any change touching the drifted vocabulary; it is not a warning to note and pass. Paired with COT-15, which records that drift was actually present.

COT-15.reason_or_evidence: Records a live drift check executed 2026-07-28 that found the committed vocabulary ALREADY drifted, with named missing values across MlsStatus (7 values), ListingPermission/Permission (ComingSoon), SyndicateTo (3) and Disclosures (OwnerIsanAgent). MlsStatus and ListingPermission drive DISPLAY GATING, so this is the concrete justification for COT-11..COT-14. NOT re-verified in this session — the recorded date and result are carried forward as the source states them, not re-probed.

COT-16.reason_or_evidence: Listing agent name, listing office name and every displayed attribution string are provider-derived and subject to COT-11: never composed locally, never defaulted, never carried forward from a stale copy when the provider row refreshes. Attribution is a NY DOS §175.25 and REBNY display-rule surface, so a stale or composed value is a compliance exposure, not a cosmetic one.

COT-17.reason_or_evidence: Field maps, enum maps and classification maps are GENERATED from live provider metadata and regenerated when the provider changes; a hand-authored mapping table is a cache subject to COT-12 and a drift check. Matches CLAUDE.md §J.6 (generated-artifact PRs must prove the generator ran).

LST-1.reason_or_evidence: A verified Mallan/provider matched pair produces exactly one Mallan public result and one canonical Mallan page. The headline invariant the whole LST family exists to protect; SEA-7 and SEA-10 criterion 15 restate it for search.

LST-2.reason_or_evidence: Mallan web edits never rewrite the Cotality/provider row. Read-only-display discipline for IDX data.

LST-3.canonical_destination: §Listings — no provider overwrite of Mallan workflow
LST-3.reason_or_evidence: Provider refreshes never erase Mallan presentation, local media, seller workflow, CRM history, marketing or notes. The converse of LST-2 and the reason provider sync must be additive.

LST-4.reason_or_evidence: SL-* = Mallan web SALE, RL-* = Mallan web RENTAL, RLS* = provider record. Explicitly warns that RL- is NOT an abbreviation of RLS: treating RL- as a provider prefix would apply Mallan-owned display handling to provider records, a compliance failure. The prefix identifies transaction type ONLY and does not establish whether a Cotality counterpart exists.

LST-5.reason_or_evidence: Seven dimensions that must be represented SEPARATELY rather than overloaded onto the prefix: transaction_type, record_source, mallan_web_id, provider_identity, reconciliation_status (6 values), public_canonical_source. This is the structural fix for the LST-9 shortcut.

LST-6.reason_or_evidence: Concrete matched-pair example (333 East 46th Street Apt 2G: SL-0004 / RLS20093870, verified_match, provider duplicate suppressed, provider row retained read-only). Kept as the canonical worked example. NOTE: `SL-0004` is a listing record identifier, not a requirement ID — recorded in the ledger's excluded table for that reason.

LST-7.reason_or_evidence: Six behaviors on verified match. Names the exact surfaces the provider duplicate must be suppressed from: public results, cards, sitemaps, canonical URLs, agent listing pages, featured listings and similar-listing results. CODE-VERIFIED that four of these have suppression wired — app/api/listings/route.ts:11, app/api/agents/[slug]/listings/route.ts:10, app/api/listings/similar/route.ts:5, app/sitemap.ts:3 — plus lib/featured/featured-ordering.ts:37 importing the address-key helper.

LST-8.reason_or_evidence: Matching does not convert the Mallan record into a provider-owned record and does not withdraw the Mallan page. Contains an explicit supersession clause: any document saying to withdraw the SL-/RL- record or replace it publicly with RLS* is superseded. That clause governs conflicts with older planning documents during this reconciliation.

LST-9.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED PRESENT: the shortcut is real and live — lib/search/public-listing-db.ts:219-223 filters `exclusive=mallan` by `listing_id startsWith "SL-"` OR `"RL-"`, using the prefix as a proxy for Mallan ownership. The source correctly labels this an implementation shortcut, not the business definition. PH-1 must inventory every prefix inference; PH-2 must replace unsafe ones with explicit source/ownership/reconciliation fields.

LST-10.reason_or_evidence: A verified match requires sufficient identity evidence (normalized address atoms, unit, postal code, listing class, known provider identity, agent/office relationship, effective dates, corroborating data). Email, a loose address string, or one coincidental attribute is explicitly not enough.

LST-11.reason_or_evidence: Possible, conflicting or broken matches may NOT suppress either record as though the match were verified; they require review. Fail-closed rule — suppressing on an unverified match would hide a legitimate listing.

LST-12.reason_or_evidence: The provider counterpart stays authoritative for its own returned facts: provider identifiers, timestamps, status, attribution, permissions and media metadata.

LST-13.reason_or_evidence: The Mallan record stays authoritative for presentation and workflow: headline, Mallan-owned media and ordering, seller portal content, marketing plan/history, notes, showings/feedback, offers/tasks, documents, CMA selection and professional adjustments, featured ordering when permitted.

LST-14.reason_or_evidence: Compare material facts on a verified pair (status, price, address/unit, listing class, public remarks, attribution, open houses, material dates, provider display permission). A discrepancy creates a VISIBLE reconciliation condition; serious public or compliance discrepancies block or degrade publication rather than being hidden.

LST-15.reason_or_evidence: CRM must let an authorized agent or broker see the pairing, inspect field-level discrepancies, confirm a possible match, reject an incorrect one, repair a broken one, and record who resolved it and when. Operator-facing counterpart to LST-11 and LST-14.

LST-16.reason_or_evidence: Source declares this OPEN, tracked as Q-3: whether the data model expresses the match relationship explicitly or infers it at query time. PARTIAL CODE EVIDENCE: prisma/schema.prisma carries `ListingIdentity`, `IdentityMatchAudit` and `IdentityReviewQueue` models, so an explicit identity layer EXISTS in schema. Whether it is populated and read on the public path was NOT verified, so the question is narrowed but not closed. Resolving it may require a schema change, which is a standing Maya-approval hold.

LST-17.reason_or_evidence: CORRECTED BY CODE READ. The source records an open doubt — 'Not verified: whether lib/search/public-listing-db.ts and lib/search/public-listing-trestle.ts apply cross-source suppression. No caller was observed in those paths.' Both files EXIST and neither imports the dedupe module, but that is not a defect: both are QUERY BUILDERS, not result pipelines. public-listing-db.ts returns {where, orderBy} (a Prisma query shape) and public-listing-trestle.ts builds an OData $filter string; neither ever sees result rows, so suppression cannot belong there. Their caller app/api/listings/route.ts imports BOTH (lines 17-18) and applies preferCrmExclusiveOverIdxDuplicate at line 441. The open doubt is therefore resolved in the architecture's favour. A SEPARATE and real defect was found in the same read — see SEA-7.

SEA-1.reason_or_evidence: Public and authenticated agent search may differ in inventory, permissions, fields, ranking and actions but share stable filter definitions and provider mappings.

SEA-2.reason_or_evidence: Public search uses only inventory and fields authorized for public display. CODE-VERIFIED SUPPORT: lib/search/public-listing-db.ts imports buildSearchDisplayWhere and SEARCH_DISPLAY_GATE from lib/search/listing-access-decision, so a display gate is applied at query-build time.

SEA-3.reason_or_evidence: Do not claim full-market or full-RLS coverage without a separately authorized feed, proved. The interface must state ACTUAL scope. Directly relevant to the external-inventory hold (OneKey / NY-State MLS), where claiming coverage before authorization would be an advertising exposure.

SEA-4.reason_or_evidence: Each visible control maps end to end across ten stages from UI control through criteria schema, application service, provider/local query, field mapping, policy decision, DTO, rendering, saved-search version and alert replay. Relevant to the deep-audit finding AUDIT-SEARCH-DUAL-RUNTIME, where the DB path and the live Cotality fallback are not semantically equivalent.

SEA-5.reason_or_evidence: Unsupported or unpermitted criteria produce an EXPLICIT decision; never silently dropped and never a silent zero. A silently dropped filter returns listings the user excluded, which on a Fair Housing-adjacent filter is a compliance exposure, not just a UX bug.

SEA-6.reason_or_evidence: Determinism holds WITHIN a fixed (criteria, audience, inventory scope, entitlement set, as-of snapshot) tuple — the source explicitly corrects the naive reading that public and agent results should match. Kept with that correction intact.

SEA-7.reason_or_evidence: CODE-VERIFIED DEFECT — the current DB path violates this ordering. SEA-7 requires identity reconciliation and public suppression BEFORE final totals, pagination, saved-search replay, sitemap output and similar-listing output. In app/api/listings/route.ts the order is inverted: pagination is applied inside the query (`skip: dbSkip, take: dbTake`, lines 332-337); the total comes from `prisma.listing.count({ where: dbWhere })` on the SAME where clause with no suppression (line 415); then filterDisplayableDbListings runs on the already-cut page (line 434) and preferCrmExclusiveOverIdxDuplicate runs after it (line 441). Consequences that follow structurally: the reported total overstates by every suppressed duplicate and non-displayable row across the full result set, and a page can return fewer than `limit` items — which SEA-10 criterion 3 ('pagination with no unreachable results') forbids. Line 1086 adjusts the total from page-local counts, which cannot correct a full-set overstatement. POL-2.reason_or_evidence: The application may load the MINIMUM record needed to evaluate policy, then applies authorization, listing restrictions, audience rules, field suppression, attribution and purpose-specific policy before returning protected data. The concession is deliberate and must survive: policy depending on record-specific facts cannot precede loading that record, and requiring every gate before every data access is not implementable. A stricter restatement would be unimplementable and would therefore be ignored.

POL-3.reason_or_evidence: Until a production scanner and workflow are connected and PROVED, the state is `not_evaluated`, NOT `allowed`. Compliance-sensitive public or marketing content requires human review when automated evaluation is unavailable or inconclusive, and `not_evaluated` is recorded ON THE ARTIFACT so anything produced while evaluation was unavailable stays identifiable afterwards. That last clause is what makes remediation possible later.

POL-4.reason_or_evidence: Fourteen attributes per operationalized policy including authority, official_source, effective_date, superseded_date, enforcement_mode and test_ids. This is the concrete answer to the deep-audit finding AUDIT-POLICY-VERSIONING: without it a display or compliance decision cannot be replayed against the rule version that produced it — which matters directly because COT-15 shows the provider vocabulary had already drifted.

POL-5.reason_or_evidence: Five surface classes requiring the POL-3 review path, with an explicit boundary: purely internal, non-client-facing text is NOT gated. The boundary is as important as the list — gating internal text would flood reviewers and train them to dismiss findings. Category 5 ('any generated text destined for any of the above') is what binds AI output to the same standard as authored copy, and it is also the enforcement point for BIZ-8's no-free-services rule.

POL-6.reason_or_evidence: A compliance evaluation receives the text, originating field, audience, surface and listing provenance — never a bare string. The stated reason must survive: without context an evaluation cannot distinguish a factual amenity description from a statement of preference about occupants, and will produce false results THAT TRAIN REVIEWERS TO IGNORE IT. A false-positive-heavy Fair Housing scanner is worse than none, because it manufactures consent to dismiss real findings.

REB-1.reason_or_evidence: REBNY controls the applicable RLS policy, participation rules, display obligations, feed rights, attribution requirements, status obligations and effective rule changes. The REBNY counterpart of COT-1, and the reason BIZ-0 must label REBNY_RLS and REBNY_UCBA obligations distinctly from NY statute.

REB-2.reason_or_evidence: A REBNY rule applies according to its effective date; historical records are interpreted under the rule in force AT THE TIME OF THE ACTION, while current disclosures follow the current rule. This is what makes BIZ-1's three separate compensation dates operationally meaningful rather than trivia, and it requires the policy versioning of POL-4 to be implementable at all.

REB-3.reason_or_evidence: Stop and report when a REBNY, RLS, IDX, display or attribution requirement is unclear, conflicting or absent from the canonical compliance source. Do not guess from memory; do not extrapolate from one field's handling to another's or from one market's behavior to another's. This is identical to CLAUDE.md §E, and the 2026-04-30 incident is exactly the extrapolation it forbids. It is also the rule this reconciliation applied when it declined to decide POL-CONFLICT-GATE34.

AUD-1.reason_or_evidence: The current count of conforming entry points is recorded once as a baseline, so conformance is measured against a real starting point rather than an aspiration.

AUD-2.reason_or_evidence: The validator fails if conformance DECREASES. New entry points must conform; existing non-conforming ones migrate at any pace but are never added to. A ratchet permits incremental progress without permitting regression — the same shape as the ucba:audit REGRESSIONS=0 hard stop in CLAUDE.md §G.

AUD-3.reason_or_evidence: Eight checks: entry-point classification, transport-exception registration, envelope conformance, explicit result state on collection responses, error-catalog conformance, generated-client drift, application-service boundary per ARC-9, and provider-vocabulary drift per COT-12. It is also where IAM-9 says a missing idempotency key on a must-not-double-apply operation is caught.

AUD-4.reason_or_evidence: The validator must state what it PROVES and what it DOES NOT: it verifies contract conformance; it does not verify correctness, authorization behavior or live operation. Identical in spirit to CLAUDE.md §J.8 ('no green-checks claim stands alone'). This ledger applies the same standard to itself via its verification_status column.

AUD-5.reason_or_evidence: An audit failure BLOCKS the change; it is not advisory output. Advisory validators are ignored under deadline pressure, which is the failure mode this row exists to prevent.

GATE-1.reason_or_evidence: A capability may not be marked complete by prose; completion is a structured claim a validator accepts or rejects. The evidence record carries method, verbatim command INCLUDING ANY WRAPPER, raw (not summarized) output, integer exit_code, target_sha, environment, observed_at, and both `proves` and `does_not_prove`. The paired proves/does_not_prove fields are the innovation — they force the boundary of a claim to be stated at the moment it is made.

GATE-2.reason_or_evidence: Twelve rejection conditions. Two encode failures this project has actually made: SOURCE_READ_FOR_BEHAVIOR (a source read cannot support a rendering or runtime claim — the FARE Act finding of 2026-05-20) and GREP_FOR_ABSENCE (a negative search asserting something does not exist rather than was not found in the searched paths — HYG-1). PLACEHOLDER_EVIDENCE enumerates the exact tokens that must be rejected: unverified, tbd, pending, todo, n/a, none.

GATE-3.canonical_destination: §Completion gate — the exit code cannot be asserted
GATE-3.reason_or_evidence: The gate's honest self-assessment, and it must not be overstated in transfer: it does NOT verify that a recorded exit code is truthful — it cannot. It makes the claim FALSIFIABLE, because command plus target_sha plus environment makes it reproducible by a third party. A false claim becomes a discoverable error rather than an unverifiable opinion. Any restatement claiming the gate verifies truthfulness would be a false claim about the gate itself.

GATE-4.reason_or_evidence: When a requirement changes, every completion claim whose evidence predates the change and whose capability depends on it is marked EVIDENCE_STALE and loses promoted status until re-evidenced. This is the enforcement arm of the change protocol: changing a decided requirement does not silently leave downstream capabilities claiming completion against a superseded rule.

GATE-5.reason_or_evidence: A search finding nothing is legitimate evidence and must record what was searched, where, and with what pattern. Its `proves` states NOT FOUND IN THE SEARCHED PATHS and may never state DOES NOT EXIST. Carries a concrete operational detail worth preserving: a bare grep finding nothing exits 1, not 0, so where 0 is recorded for a no-match search the wrapper that produced it must be visible in `command`. This ledger's own negative findings (e.g. RESOURCE_NOT_AVAILABLE, acting_capacity) are phrased to this standard.

GATE-6.canonical_destination: §Completion gate — the gate states its own limits
GATE-6.reason_or_evidence: It proves every promoted status carries a complete, well-formed, anchored evidence record. It does NOT prove any recorded output is truthful, that any test passes, that anything works in production, or that the capability inventory is complete. 'A green gate means the claims are honest in FORM. Substance is established by the evidence itself and by review.' That sentence should transfer verbatim.

GATE-7.reason_or_evidence: DERIVED from AUD-2. The count of capabilities passing the gate is a baseline and the gate fails if it decreases, so a capability may not be QUIETLY DEMOTED to avoid producing evidence. Without this clause the gate is trivially defeated by lowering a claim instead of evidencing it.

GATE-8.reason_or_evidence: The gate runs from one named command, reports per-capability results and exits non-zero on any rejection, converging into platform:check (HYG-8). This is the row that connects the completion gate to PR #579's capability-audit machinery, so it must be decided ONCE across both unmerged lines.

HYG-1.reason_or_evidence: The absence of a discovered caller is not proof that a route, module, field, flag, job or document is safe to remove. Directly constrains this reconciliation: several rows here record 'no caller observed', and under HYG-1 none of them authorizes a deletion. It is also why BIZ-10.2 requires classification before any compensation-field removal.

HYG-2.reason_or_evidence: Sixteen bloat categories including duplicate architecture documents (the condition this reconciliation exists to end), duplicate media or listing rows without reconciliation, and copied provider facts that become conflicting local truth. Closes with a protection that must survive: HISTORICAL MIGRATIONS ARE NOT BLOAT and must not be deleted merely to make the repository smaller.

HYG-3.reason_or_evidence: Eight cleanup states: KEEP_ACTIVE, MIGRATE, CONSOLIDATE, EVIDENCE_ONLY, HISTORICAL, DEPRECATE_AFTER_PROOF, DELETE_AFTER_PROOF, UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE. The two AFTER_PROOF states and UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE are what stop a cleanup pass from becoming a deletion pass. Structurally the same device as this ledger's disposition column, where `unresolved` plays the UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_TRACE role.

HYG-4.reason_or_evidence: Twelve machine-readable or GENERATED inventories: normative documents, routes and methods, non-HTTP entry points, errors, flags, environment variables, crons and jobs, provider adapters, database models and fields, public assets, dependencies, temporary compatibility code. Generated rather than authored is the operative word — AUDIT-GOVERNANCE-DRIFT showed hand-authored counts drift.

HYG-5.reason_or_evidence: Every temporary item records owner, reason, introduced_at, removal_condition, latest_review_date and a test proving safe removal. 'There is no permanent temporary code.' Directly applicable to the in-flight media migration, where Listing.media remains the read path until the PR 4 reader swap — a temporary compatibility path that currently has no recorded deadline.

HYG-6.reason_or_evidence: Eight ordered steps before removal. Step 2 is the load-bearing one — DISTINGUISH 'no caller found in searched paths' FROM 'unused' — and steps 3-5 require replacement behavior, proof of it, and preserved rollback BEFORE the old path is removed. This is the procedure that makes HYG-1 actionable rather than merely prohibitive.

HYG-7.reason_or_evidence: Seven questions every PR answers, ending with 'What proves no unrelated files were included?' — which is the check that makes HYG-9 and OPS-6 verifiable rather than aspirational.

HYG-8.reason_or_evidence: A progressive `npm run platform:check` converging on twelve validations. Explicitly a TARGET, not a claim of current state, and it carries its own honesty clause: the command must state what it currently proves and what remains planned. Converging point for GATE-8 and the PR #579 capability audit, so the two must not be built twice.

HYG-9.reason_or_evidence: A branch contains one bounded capability; unrelated in-flight work is never swept into a commit; the staged set is inspected against intended scope before every commit. This reconciliation is being conducted in an isolated worktree for exactly this reason, leaving the Phase 1A and primary checkouts undisturbed.

DOC-1.reason_or_evidence: Only the canonical plan may establish platform-wide architecture, business rules, implementation sequence or cross-system contracts. This is the requirement that makes the PR #585 / PR #579 reconciliation mandatory rather than optional — two normative plans cannot both satisfy DOC-1.

DOC-2.reason_or_evidence: AGENTS.md, AI-START-HERE.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md and README.md must identify the canonical plan as the first platform-plan read. They MAY summarize or route but MAY NOT duplicate a competing architecture. This is the exact decision the reconciliation must make for PR #585's four governance files and PR #579's four — route, do not duplicate.
DOC-2.dependency: DOC-1, PR#585 governance files, PR#579 governance files

DOC-3.reason_or_evidence: Names the exact forbidden filenames — PLAN-REV6, -FINAL, -NEW, -YYYY-MM-DD, -ADDENDUM. 'The path is stable. The contents evolve.' Identical in force to the source-of-truth charter's no-parallel-file rule, and it governs the output of this reconciliation: the result must be the SAME path, amended, not a new dated plan.

DOC-4.reason_or_evidence: Names seven documents that contain useful requirements or evidence but must not remain competing normative plans, INCLUDING Mallan_Intelligence_Master_Plan.md — which is PR #579's plan. Prescribes exactly the seven-column coverage record this ledger implements (source_file, source_section, source_requirement, accepted|corrected|rejected|historical|evidence_only, master_plan_destination, verification_source, notes). Retirement means the file no longer calls itself authoritative; git history preserves it. This row is the specification this ledger is built to satisfy.

DOC-5.reason_or_evidence: A change to a decided requirement must recheck every dependent requirement, README summary, agent instruction, active issue and handoff affected by it. GATE-4 is the machine enforcement of this rule; without GATE-4 it depends on diligence alone.

DOC-6.reason_or_evidence: No source document is retired until its coverage matrix row EXISTS and states where each requirement landed. Applied literally to this reconciliation: neither PR #585's plan nor PR #579's plan may be retired until every one of their sections has a resolved ledger row. As of this batch 460 rows remain unresolved, so no retirement is authorized.

DOC-7.reason_or_evidence: Coverage matrices, conflict decisions, open questions, retired-document lists, requirement indexes and change history live in the plan's appendices and do not become separate documents. TENSION TO RESOLVE: this ledger and its resolutions file are currently separate documents. They are working artefacts of the reconciliation rather than appendices of the finished plan, but DOC-7 requires the final canonical plan to absorb the coverage matrix, conflict decisions and open questions. Recorded here so the final assembly step cannot overlook it.
DOC-7.dependency: DOC-4, DOC-6, final canonical plan assembly

DOC-8.reason_or_evidence: A withdrawn requirement KEEPS its identifier, marked RETIRED, with reason and replacement recorded; the identifier is NEVER REASSIGNED. This prevents the worst reconciliation failure mode — an identifier silently coming to mean something different, so that older evidence and audits appear to support a requirement they never addressed.

OPS-1.reason_or_evidence: A capability is not complete without exact tests, production or immutable-preview proof, health evidence, rollback, documentation and operational ownership. The source itself observes that OPS-1 was never enforced — 'an agent can write done and nothing stops it' — which is why the GATE family exists. Retained as the statement of the rule; GATE-1..GATE-8 are its enforcement.

OPS-2.reason_or_evidence: Seven elements per claim: what was checked, exact command, raw output, exit code, exact commit and environment, what the evidence proves, what it does not prove. 'Three of these are not sufficient.' Identical to CLAUDE.md §F and to the memory/EVIDENCE-STANDARD-2026-07-27.md artefact that PR #579 also carries — so this rule exists on BOTH unmerged lines and must be decided once.

OPS-3.reason_or_evidence: Nine applicable layers from pure contract and unit tests through preview or production smoke tests, health probes and data reconciliation queries. The breadth matters: OPS-024 passed 5,814 unit tests because every fixture fabricated ListingKey, so unit coverage alone cannot establish provider-contract correctness.

OPS-4.reason_or_evidence: Production proof includes deployed commit, deployment identity, exact endpoint or workflow, timestamp, observed response or behavior, and relevant logs or queries. 'A source read or a passing unit test never substitutes for a rendering or behavior claim.' This is precisely why TXN-10's FARE render is left unverified in this ledger — no live probe was run.

OPS-5.reason_or_evidence: Every implementation PR states the rollback procedure AND verifies that rollback does not corrupt data, identity, policy or audit history. The second clause is the one usually skipped and the one OPS-024 exercised for real: recovery required both a Vercel rollback and a revert of main.

OPS-6.reason_or_evidence: Each branch and PR contains one bounded capability, diffed against its intended base before push and before merge. Same requirement as HYG-9; combined onto HYG-9 as the canonical statement so the rule is not maintained in two places, with OPS-6 retained as the operations-side reference.

OPS-7.reason_or_evidence: No merge or production release occurs without Maya's approval. Matches the standing holds in CLAUDE.md §C and governs the disposition of every deferred_with_gate row in this ledger. It is also the rule under which this branch remains unpushed.

OPS-8.reason_or_evidence: Operational probes proving the affected surface responds correctly are run BEFORE AND AFTER a change, with output recorded. The before-probe is what distinguishes a regression from a pre-existing condition — the distinction OPS-025 needed in order to be classified as pre-existing rather than Phase 1A damage.
